How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

We need to respond with instructions or code snippet. We can use the provided function to call the API. The function expects url and fabricName. The default URL includes placeholder. We need to replace <ip> with 192.168.11.33 and fabricName with PEK-ACI. So URL: https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI. Then we can call the function. But the user might just want instructions. We can show how to construct the request using curl or python requests. Provide example code. Also mention authentication (likely token). Provide steps: 1) Get auth token via login API. 2) Use token in Authorization header. 3) Make GET request to above URL. Provide sample curl command: curl -k -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI. Or python requests: import requests; headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'}; r=requests.get(url, headers=headers, verify=False). Then parse JSON.

We can also call the function to demonstrate. Let's do that.
